conclusions.question: On engine 1.2.0, is a compound TTL index rejected, and with what error?
conclusions.answer: Yes. createIndexes {key: {a: 1, b: 1}, name: 'ab_ttl', expireAfterSeconds: 5} fails with code 67 CannotCreateIndex, errmsg "Error in specification { "key" : { "a" : 1, "b" : 1 }, "name" : "ab_ttl", "expireAfterSeconds" : 5 }:TTL indexes work only on single fields, and compound indexes are incompatible with TTL functionality.", and the reply carries no errorLabels key. Code, codeName and rule text are identical to engine 0.117, and both 1.2.0 runs gave the same reply. A non-numeric expireAfterSeconds ('abc') is likewise rejected with code 67 CannotCreateIndex ("The 'expireAfterSeconds' option for a TTL index must be a numeric value, but a different data type was provided: string."), also unchanged from 0.117. Evidence is from documentdb-local 1.2.0, not the managed service.

conclusions.question: Can one collection carry a second single-field TTL index, and does that index expire documents on its own?
conclusions.answer: Yes. exp2_ttl was accepted next to exp_ttl (numIndexesAfter 3). Both documents carrying a past Date in exp2 were deleted by the first pg_cron run after the index existed (2026-11-25T21:01:00.026999Z, lag 55.0 s): exp2_past_only has no exp field, and exp_future_exp2_past has exp one day in the future. The control document with exp2 a day in the future survived. So each TTL index expires documents independently, and an index built after the documents were inserted still purges them. The 0.117 run created exp2_ttl but no document carried exp2, so the purge itself is new evidence. Building exp2_ttl on the 10-document collection took 2006 ms (run 1: 1009.0 ms; 0.117: 2.01 s), against about 17 ms for exp_ttl on the empty collection.

conclusions.question: Which values of a TTL-indexed field expire (Date, string, number, null, missing, array)?
conclusions.answer: Only BSON Dates. A Date 60 s in the past was deleted. So was an array holding one past Date and one Date a day ahead, so any expired element expires the document. An ISO-8601 string, a 64-bit integer epoch-milliseconds value, null and a missing field were never deleted. They survived 4 TTL runs over a 242.0 s window (3 runs in run 1), exactly as on 0.117. This turns the DECISIONS topic-10 statement that numbers, strings and missing fields are not deleted, recorded there as an inference from the Date-typed $lt predicate in ttl_index.c, into an observation for open-source engines 0.117 and 1.2.0.

conclusions.question: What is the TTL purge cadence and lag on engine 1.2.0 with open-source defaults?
conclusions.answer: pg_cron job documentdb_ttl_task, schedule '* * * * *', command CALL documentdb_api_internal.delete_expired_rows(); (cron.timezone GMT). cron.job_run_details shows 7 runs, each starting 5 to 27 ms after a whole minute and lasting 1.9 to 4.8 ms, all with status succeeded. Every expired document was deleted by the first run after it became eligible (all 7 documents; 0 eligible-but-skipped runs). Lags from eligibility (field time + 5 s, or insert or index creation if later) to the purging run: array_of_dates 57.0 s, exp2_past_only 55.0 s, exp_future_exp2_past 55.0 s, past_date_60s 57.0 s, future_date_90s 22.0 s, probe2_past_date 54.9 s, probe3_past_date 54.9 s. That is the time to the next whole minute, so expect 0 to about 60 s plus milliseconds. 0.117 was the same: one run a minute at hh:mm:00.003 to .016, lags of about 60, 25, 58 and 58 s.

conclusions.question: Did TTL behaviour change between engine 0.117 and engine 1.2.0?
conclusions.answer: Not in anything this test measures. The compound-TTL and non-numeric errors are the same, the second TTL index is accepted, and the listIndexes entry is the same: {"v": 2, "key": {"exp": 1}, "name": "exp_ttl", "expireAfterSeconds": 5, "storageEngine": {"enableOrderedIndex": true}}. The same values expire, the purge still runs once a minute through pg_cron, and the lag is still first-run-after-eligibility. Two settings exist on 1.2.0. documentdb.enable_ttl_cleanup_background=off is a background-worker TTL path that is off by default, so pg_cron still purges. documentdb.createTTLIndexAsCompositeByDefault=on selects composite-term index op classes for TTL indexes; in create_indexes.c it does not relax the single-field rule. Whether these settings also existed on 0.117 is unknown, because PostgreSQL had crashed before they could be read there.

conclusions.question: Does the spec's command docker exec ddb-engine-test psql -U postgres -p 9712 -tAc "select jobname, schedule, command from cron.job" work on 1.2.0?
conclusions.answer: No. It exits 2 with: psql: error: connection to server on socket "/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.9712" failed: FATAL:  role "postgres" does not exist. The image runs PostgreSQL as OS user documentdb, and documentdb is both the superuser and the owner of the pg_cron jobs. psql -U documentdb -p 9712 -d postgres works and lists 4 jobs: documentdb_ttl_task (* * * * *): CALL documentdb_api_internal.delete_expired_rows(); documentdb_index_build_task_1 (2 seconds): CALL documentdb_api_internal.build_index_concurrently(1); documentdb_index_build_task_2 (2 seconds): CALL documentdb_api_internal.build_index_concurrently(2); documentdb_cursor_cleanup_task (* * * * *): SELECT documentdb_api_internal.cursor_directory_cleanup(). The list is identical after the TTL indexes are created, so there is no per-index job. Whether 0.117 had a postgres role is unknown, because its PostgreSQL had crashed before the read.

conclusions.question: Does this settle the managed service's TTL purge cadence (DECISIONS topic 10, open item 5)?
conclusions.answer: No. It establishes only the open-source 1.2.0 defaults: a per-minute pg_cron job, plus these settings, all with source=default in pg_settings: TTLTaskMaxRunTimeInMS=60000, repeatPurgeIndexesForTTLTask=on, maxTTLDeleteBatchSize=1000, SingleTTLTaskTimeBudget=20000 and TTLPurgerStatementTimeout=60000. With repeatPurgeIndexesForTTLTask on, each run repeats delete batches until a pass deletes nothing or 60 s pass (ttl_index.c), which matches the release note's 'continuous for up to 60 seconds'. On this tiny collection every run ended within milliseconds, so the 60 s continuous mode was never exercised. The managed cluster's settings and schedule cannot be seen from here. Keep the kit wording 'expiry lags by up to about a minute after the field's time plus expireAfterSeconds; not exact'.

conclusions.question: Incidental: what shape do the gateway's createIndexes and drop replies have on 1.2.0?
conclusions.answer: createIndexes nests its counts the way a sharded router does: {"raw": {"defaultShard": {"numIndexesBefore": 1, "numIndexesAfter": 2, "createdCollectionAutomatically": true, "ok": 1}}, "ok": 1}. hello reports msg 'isdbgrid'. A kit helper that reads numIndexesAfter at the top level gets nothing; it should look under raw.<shard>. The 0.117 TTL test used create_index, which returns only the index name, so there is no 0.117 reply to compare. Dropping a collection that does not exist yet returns {"ok": 1.0, "dropped": "docs"}, as on 0.117.

notes: Evidence scope: documentdb-local ghcr.io/documentdb/documentdb/documentdb-local:pg17-1.2.0 (OCI version 1.2.0, revision 965b6e7ad1c4, image sha256:1d40546ccf53...), extension documentdb 1.2-0, gateway buildInfo.version 7.0.0; hello also reports internal.documentdb_versions ["1.2-0", "1.2.0"]. It shows open-source engine behaviour at this version with default settings, not managed Azure DocumentDB behaviour.

Two independent runs on 1.2.0 gave the same results. run 1 (report.run1.json, run1.log) is a 226 s window, because a deadline bug dropped its last poll; run 2 (this report) is the full 17-poll, 242 s window. Same purged set, same survivors, same errors.

Setup is held away from the pg_cron minute (setupPhaseGuard): if it would start within 10 s before or 2 s after a whole minute, the script waits until hh:mm:03. So in both runs the documents were inserted at about hh:mm:03, which is why the already-expired documents show lags of about 55 to 57 s.

The container was shared with other 1.2.0 reruns running at the same time (pgvector 'ivfflat index created with little data' notices from another test appear in the PostgreSQL log). /data had 11 GB free before and after, and every TTL run succeeded within milliseconds.

The script ran the spec's exact psql -U postgres command and recorded its error; the pg_cron schedule was then read as role documentdb. All psql reads were SELECTs on cron.job, cron.job_run_details, pg_extension and pg_settings.
Database t_ttl was dropped at the end ({ok: 1, dropped: 't_ttl'}) and is no longer listed. No other database was touched, and the container was left running.
